ledger.x: 1 December 1918: Transylvania unites with Romania and Greater Romania is complete.
ledger.cpn: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia (Principality and Kingdom of Romania to 1918)

ledger.x: 16 April 1919: the Romanian offensive against Hungary begins ('The Romanian offensive began on 16 April 1919'); 'By the evening of 1 May, the entire east bank of the Tisza River was under the control of the Romanian Army.'
3 August 1919: the war ends in a Romanian victory.
August 1919: Romania occupies Budapest and, in the page's words, 'occupied all of Hungary except for an area around Lake Balaton'.
Early 1920: 'In early 1920, Romanian troops departed Hungary.'

4 June 1920: the Treaty of Trianon, signed 'on 4 June 1920' and in force 26 July 1921, gives Romania 'all of Transylvania, which was home to 2,800,000 Romanians'; 'The central parts of Banat were later assigned to Romania' (Crisana and Maramures are not named on the page, so the region is the researcher's reading).
1940: the country's name is changed to Legionary Romania (the National Legionary State); the page gives no month.
28 June 1940: the Soviet Union occupies Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina.
30 August 1940: the Second Vienna Award gives Hungary Northern Transylvania.
7 September 1940: Romania cedes Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria by the Treaty of Craiova.
22 June 1941: Romania joins the German attack on the Soviet Union.
26 July 1941: Bessarabia, Northern Bukovina and Hertsa are back in Axis hands.
July 1941: Romania retakes Bessarabia, Northern Bukovina and Hertsa.
19 August 1941: the Transnistria Governorate is established under Romanian administration (Odessa fell on 16 October 1941).
March 1944: the Romanian administration of Transnistria ends.
August 1944: the Soviet Second Jassy-Kishinev Offensive reaches Bessarabia ('In August 1944, during the Soviet Second Jassy-Kishinev Offensive ...
August 1944: the Soviet Union retakes Bessarabia, Northern Bukovina and Hertsa; the 1947 border treaty later 'confirmed the border fixed in 1940'.
12 September 1944: the armistice ends the fighting.
25 October 1944: Northern Transylvania is back.
October 1944: Northern Transylvania is under Romanian and Soviet control.
9 March 1945: the Soviet administration of Northern Transylvania ends.
30 December 1947: King Michael I abdicates and the Romanian People's Republic is proclaimed ('Republic proclaimed: 30 December 1947').

wars.name: Hungarian-Romanian War
wars.outcome: Romanian victory: the Romanian Army reached Budapest on 4 August 1919 and 'occupied all of Hungary except for an area around Lake Balaton'; its troops left in early 1920 and Trianon fixed the frontier.

wars.name: Soviet occupation of Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina
wars.outcome: Romania yields Bessarabia, Northern Bukovina and Hertsa (50,762 km2) to an ultimatum of 26 June 1940 and the Soviet occupation of 28 June - 3 July.

wars.name: Romania in the Eastern Front, 1941-1944
wars.outcome: Romania retook Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina in July 1941 and administered Transnistria from 19 August 1941; the Soviet Second Jassy-Kishinev Offensive of August 1944 and the coup of 23 August ended it, with the armistice of 12 September 1944.

certainty.note: The union of Bessarabia, Bukovina and Transylvania was declared in 1918 and the Banat and Hungarian frontiers were still moving until Trianon; the Romanian army was in Hungary in 1919.
Trianon, Saint-Germain and the Treaty of Paris (Bessarabia, recognised by some powers only) fixed the frontiers.

Ultimatums, the Vienna Award and Craiova gave sharp lines in 1940 (Vienna Award and Craiova are dated treaties), but the Soviet frontier of 1940-41 and 1944 and the Transnistria Governorate are approximate.
Frontiers of 1 January 1941 with Northern Transylvania restored, confirmed in the 1947 Paris treaties.
